decisions.reason: As a close extension of the firm's core dosimetry and QA capabilities that remained prominent on the home page in both 2023 and 2024, it fits existing knowledge well and offers strong scope for incremental improvement through the firm's R&D and service base.

This oncology risk management software builds directly on the firm's established clinical QA and integration expertise, and its continued dedicated presentation across two years suggests enough early traction for the firm to keep learning and refining it.

A CT image quality test phantom is closely related to the firm's medical imaging QA activities, so the firm is likely to retain it because its existing measurement know-how and research links should make commercialization and product improvement manageable.

Although adjacent to medical imaging, this mammography phantom is marked as distant from the firm's established offer, and with only very early market evidence the absorptive-capacity logic favors reallocating resources to products that draw more directly on the firm's stronger knowledge base.

This full field mammography test phantom also sits relatively far from the firm's core radiation therapy and integrated QA strengths, so without stronger evidence of traction the firm would likely focus its development effort on areas where it can learn and improve faster.

Medical imaging QA instruments build on the firm's existing instrumentation, calibration, and support capabilities, making them a natural area to keep while leveraging in-house R&D and customer feedback to deepen the product line.
